statement.definition: Continuous (Lipschitz) functions on sequentially compact metric spaces (M,d), M subset of Baire space, have a supremum as a sequence (2.8, 2.9) or as a function (2.14).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.11 (ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND): 2.8 and 2.9 restricted to [0,1]-valued functions are equivalent to BOOT. Corollary 2.13: BOOT+QF-AC^{0,1} iff QF-AC^{0,1}_fin + 2.9. Theorem 2.16: 2.14 implies BOOT2. Theorem 2.19: the supremum functional is equivalent to (exists^3) together with (exists^2).

statement.notation: compact metric spaces are separable; sequentially compact implies bounded
statement.name: Metric-space statements without codes
statement.definition: For metric d on N^N x N^N, sequentially compact (M,d) is separable / bounded / countably compact.
statement.facts: Separability implies BOOT and QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.2, ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND); boundedness (with QF-AC^{0,1}_fin) is equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.4, ACA_0^omega).

statement.name: Open sets in sequentially compact metric spaces are countable unions of open balls
statement.definition: Open sets (resp. with continuous modulus, with R2-representation) of a sequentially compact (M,d), M subset of Baire space, are countable unions of open balls.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.24: each implies BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND.

statement.notation: countable sets can be enumerated; measure zero
statement.name: Countable and measure zero sets in metric spaces
statement.definition: Countable (injective Y on A) sets in metric spaces on Baire space can be enumerated / are effectively measure zero.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.6: the enumeration and effectively-measure-zero statements are equivalent to BOOT+QF-AC^{0,1} (ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND); Theorem 2.7: for strongly countable sets they are equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (ACA_0^omega).

statement.name: Intermediate value theorem on sequentially compact chain connected metric spaces
statement.definition: Continuous f on a sequentially compact chain connected (M,d) with f(w)<c<f(v) takes the value c.
statement.facts: Equivalent (with the finite choice axiom) to QF-AC^{0,1->1} for M subset of N (Theorem 3.6, ACA_0^omega), to QF-AC^{0,1} for M subset of N^N (Corollary 3.7).

statement.notation: total ordering of the reals (x ≤ y ∨ y < x)
statement.name: Total ordering of the reals
statement.definition: For all real numbers x, y, x ≤ y or y < x. Used as the example of an instance reduction: given a binary sequence α, build the real x = lim 2^{-min{k | αk=1 or k=n}} and decide x ≤ 0 or 0 < x.
statement.facts: The paper states (1.1) that the total ordering of reals implies LPO (constructively, via an instance reduction). The principle has no catalogue id, so the fact (over bish) is not entered.

statement.name: There is a function not in Baire class 2
statement.definition: There is a function f : [0,1] -> R which is not the pointwise limit of Baire class 1 functions on [0,1] (Baire class 1 read as: a point of continuity of the induced function on each perfect set).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.4: RCA_0^omega proves Baire -> NIN.

statement.name: Sequential version of Baire's characterisation theorem for Baire class 1
statement.definition: For a sequence (f_n) of Baire class 1 functions with limit f there is a sequence (g_{m,n}) of continuous functions with lim_m g_{m,n} = f_n for each n (and lim_n lim_m g_{m,n} = f).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.6: RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} proves Baire' -> NIN.

statement.name: Unordered sums with the Cauchy criterion are series
statement.definition: If (a_x)_{x in [0,1]} is Cauchy (Definition 3.8) and non-negative, there is a sequence of reals (y_i) in [0,1] such that a_y = 0 whenever y differs from every y_i.
statement.facts: Provable from BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (said readily proved, based on [43, 3.2]). Theorem 3.10: RCA_0^omega + IND proves SUM -> NIN. Corollary 3.11: RCA_0^omega + IND proves SUM -> cocode0.

statement.name: Unordered sums with summability are series
statement.definition: If (a_x)_{x in [0,1]} is summable (the net limit of finite sums exists, Definition 3.7) and non-negative, there is a sequence of reals (y_i) in [0,1] such that a_y = 0 whenever y differs from every y_i (assuming (exists^2)).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.13: ACA_0^omega + IND proves SUM' -> NBI, and ACA_0^omega proves QF-AC^{0,1} -> SUM'. Corollary 3.14: ACA_0^omega + IND proves SUM' -> cocode1.

statement.name: Countably compact metric subspaces of [0,1] are separable
statement.definition: For any M subset of [0,1], if (M,d) is a countably-compact metric space (Definitions 3.15, 3.16) then it is separable (Definition 3.17).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.21: RCA_0^omega proves STS+ -> cocode0. Corollary 3.22: Pi^1_1-CA_0^omega + STS+ proves Pi^1_2-CA_0.

statement.name: Local equivalence of sequential and epsilon-delta continuity in metric spaces
statement.definition: For a metric space (M,d) with M a subset of Baire space (modulo coding), for any x in M and F : M -> M, if F is sequentially continuous at x then F is continuous at x.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.18: RCA_0^omega proves that NBI follows from it; ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} proves it. Corollary 3.19: the first part holds with net continuity in place of continuity.

statement.name: Induction axiom for all formulas of L_omega
statement.definition: The induction axiom for all formulas of the language L_omega (used as an extra hypothesis in Theorems 3.10, 3.13).
statement.facts: Used as additional axiom over RCA_0^omega and ACA_0^omega in Theorems 3.10, 3.13 and Corollaries 3.11, 3.14.

statement.name: Restricted weak continuity for numbers
statement.loc: Section 1, after Baire's theorem for B (schemata WC-N′ and BT′)
statement.definition: WC-N restricted to formulas A(α,n) of the form ∀k (σ(α(k),n)=0) with σ: N* × N → N satisfying σ(a,m)=0 ∧ m≤n → σ(a,n)=0 (increasing sequence of closed sets X_n = Π⁰₁ subsets of Baire space): ∀α∃n A(α,n) → ∀α∃n∃m∀â∈α(m) A(â,n).
statement.facts: Theorem 8: in Bishop's constructive mathematics (with countable choice, formalizable in EL or HAω with Π⁰₁-AC00) WC-N′ is equivalent to BT′ + ¬LPO and to BD-N + ¬LPO. Proposition 1: WC-N′ implies BT′ + ¬LPO. Theorem 7: BD-N + ¬LPO implies WC-N′. Not entered: the hypotheses involve ¬LPO, which has no catalogue id.

statement.name: Restricted Baire theorem for Baire space
statement.loc: Section 1, schemata WC-N and BT, restricted to increasing closed sequences
statement.definition: For A(α,n) ≡ ∀k (σ(α(k),n)=0) with σ increasing in n as in (1): ∀α∃n A(α,n) → ∃n∃a∀â∈a A(â,n) (if closed sets X_n cover B, some X_n has inhabited interior).
statement.facts: Proposition 2: BT′ implies BD-N (constructively, using countable choice only in the ambient system). Not constructively provable since BD-N is not derivable in E-HA^ω + AC (Lietz); classically true. Part of Theorem 8: BT′ + ¬LPO is equivalent to BD-N + ¬LPO and to WC-N′. Not entered as a fact because BT′ is not in the catalogue.

statement.name: The unit interval is not height-width countable
statement.definition: A set B ⊂ R is height-width countable if there are a height function H: R→N and a width function g: N→N such that B_n={x∈B: H(x)<n} is finite with size bound g(n); NIN'_alt says [0,1] is not height-width countable.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.20 (over ACA₀^ω + FIN): equivalent to many statements on BV functions (positive unordered sums with a bound or Cauchy modulus have a zero, BV and Waterman-BV functions have a continuity point, etc.). Theorem 3.15: implied by the Jordan decomposition theorem, HBU restricted to BV functions and WHBU restricted to BV functions (over ACA₀^ω + FIN). Theorem 3.22: equivalent to Fourier series of BV functions converging to f at some point. It is implied by NINalt.

statement.name: Basic properties of finite sets (finite union theorem, enumeration of finite sets, finite axiom of choice)
statement.definition: Finite union theorem for sequences of finite sets (finite in the sense of Definition 1.2), every finite set of reals is included in a finite sequence of reals, and a finite axiom of choice for Y^2 on 2^N.
statement.facts: Used as an extra axiom in the base of Theorems 3.6-3.9, 3.15, 3.20 and 3.22; derivable from a fragment of induction. Its own reverse mathematics is left open.

statement.notation: Regulated-function statements (Volterra's theorem and corollary, point of continuity, Cf dense, Blumberg's theorem, Bourbaki's Riemann integral criterion, FTC for regulated functions, Darboux points)
statement.name: Properties of regulated functions equivalent to NINalt
statement.definition: Third-order statements about regulated functions f: [0,1]→R (left and right limits everywhere), such as: f has a point of continuity; the set of continuity points is dense; there is no regulated function continuous exactly on Q∩[0,1]; Blumberg's theorem restricted to regulated functions.
statement.facts: Equivalent to NINalt over ACA₀^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + FIN (also with restrictions to Baire 2, Baire 1*, usco, lsco, supremum functional, symmetric continuity, fragmented, B-measurable of class 1 functions). Section 3.5: with the extra condition Baire 1 they become provable in ACA₀^ω + FIN + QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.notation: Existence of a modulus of regularity (Lipschitz F: [0,1] -> R with a zero)
statement.name: Existence of moduli of regularity
statement.definition: Every continuous F on a compact metric space with a zero has a modulus of regularity w.r.t. zer F (Definition 2.1).
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (Theorem 4.4.1); already for Lipschitz F on [0,1] with a zero it implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.4.2).

statement.notation: Regularity of F w.r.t. zer F (forall-epsilon-exists-delta form)
statement.name: Regularity of continuous functions with a zero
statement.definition: Every continuous F: X -> R on a compact metric space with a zero is regular w.r.t. zer F (Definition 2.1, without a modulus function).
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 (Theorem 4.2.1); already for Lipschitz F on [0,1] it implies WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.2.2).

statement.notation: Existence of a modulus of uniqueness / uniform uniqueness of the zero
statement.name: Moduli of uniqueness and uniform uniqueness
statement.definition: Every continuous F: X -> R on a compact metric space with at most one zero has a modulus of uniqueness, form (*) (Definition 2.3).
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 (Theorem 4.1.1); uniform uniqueness of the zero already for Lipschitz F on [0,1] with exactly one zero implies WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.1.2).

statement.name: Enumeration principle for height-countable sets
statement.definition: A height-countable set in [0,1] can be enumerated.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.8 (over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}): equivalent to Bernstein-polynomial and discontinuity-set statements for regulated functions and to Jordan decomposition for BV on R; ACA0^omega + enum proves ATR0 (cited from [64]).

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for measure
statement.definition: If (X_n) is an increasing sequence of measure zero closed sets of reals in [0,1], then the union has measure zero.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.15 (over ACA0^omega + INDR + QF-AC^{0,1}): equivalent to Vitali-Lebesgue and Bernstein convergence almost everywhere for Riemann integrable functions; Theorem 3.1: ACA0^omega + PHP[0,1] is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA0.

statement.name: Baire category theorem for the unit interval (third-order)
statement.definition: If (O_n) is a decreasing sequence of dense open sets of reals in [0,1], then the intersection is non-empty.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.17 (over ACA0^omega): equivalent to C_f nonempty for usco functions and to B_f nonempty for usco or cliquish functions.

statement.name: Contraposed Helly selection principle
statement.definition: For a sequence of BV functions [0,1]->[0,1] with pointwise limit not in BV, there is unbounded g with g(n) <= V(f_n) <= g(n)+1.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.8(g): with Jordan decomposition for BV into non-decreasing functions on R it is equivalent to enum; Theorem 3.10: over ACA0^omega + Helly, NIN_alt is equivalent to statements on BV functions.

statement.name: Uniform Bernstein approximation of continuous functions
statement.definition: For continuous f:[0,1]->R and x in (0,1), f(x) = lim B_n(f,x), the convergence being uniform.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0^omega (Theorem 2.1); the version for cadlag, U0-functions, and (with QF-AC^{0,1}) regulated or locally bounded functions, with limit (f(x+)+f(x-))/2, is also equivalent to WKL0 (Theorem 2.3); the existence of f and x with f(x) != lim B_n(f,x) is equivalent to (exists^2) (Theorem 2.5).

statement.name: Bernstein/continuity statements for regulated functions
statement.definition: E.g. for regulated f:[0,1]->R there is x in (0,1) where f is continuous (resp. f(x)=lim B_n(f,x)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to NIN_alt over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5).

statement.notation: Every permutably convergent series in R is absolutely convergent
statement.name: Riemann permutation theorem for series (permutable convergence implies absolute convergence)
statement.definition: A real series sum a_n is permutably convergent if every permutation of N+ gives a convergent series sum a_sigma(n). The statement: every permutably convergent series of real numbers is absolutely convergent (classically equivalent to Riemann's two series theorems).
statement.facts: Theorem 7: in BISH + BD-N, every permutably convergent series of real numbers is absolutely convergent, i.e. BD-N implies it over BISH (stated as a consequence in the introduction and Section 5). Not equivalent to BD-N: by Diener and Lubarsky [8], topological models satisfy it without BD-N, and it is not provable in the Aczel-Rathjen formulation of BISH.

statement.notation: (*) Every weak-permutably convergent series in R is absolutely convergent
statement.name: Absolute convergence of weak-permutably convergent series
statement.definition: A series sum a_n is weak-permutably convergent if it is convergent and for each permutation sigma of N+ there exists a convergent bracketing (grouping of consecutive terms along a strictly increasing f with f(1)=1) of sum a_sigma(n). The statement (*) says every such series is absolutely convergent. Classically weak-permutable convergence and permutable convergence are equivalent.
statement.facts: Theorem 8: (*) implies BD-N over BISH (via Lemma 9, which builds from an inhabited countable pseudobounded S a weak-permutably convergent series whose convergence of sum a_n forces S bounded). Hence over BISH: (*) implies BD-N implies 'every permutably convergent series is absolutely convergent'; by the Diener-Lubarsky models neither implication reverses, so weak-permutable convergence is constructively strictly weaker than permutable convergence. Proposition 1: every convergent bracketing of a rearrangement of a weak-permutably convergent series with sum s converges to s.

statement.name: Uniform continuity of RM-continuous (associate-coded) functions on Cantor space
statement.definition: (forall alpha^1)[(forall beta <=_1 1)(exists N^0) alpha(beta N)>0 -> (exists k^0)(forall beta <=_1 1)(exists N<=k) alpha(beta N)>0]: every function on Cantor space given by an associate is uniformly continuous (Simpson IV.2.2 for Cantor space).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.1: over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{2,1}, URC <-> RC <-> WKL; RC <-> WKL is straightforward (second-order, Simpson IV.2.2). Corollary 4.2: RC2, URC2, RB, URB are likewise equivalent to WKL over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{2,1}.

statement.name: Generalisations of RC, URC to compact subspaces {beta <=_1 gamma} of Baire space, and boundedness versions
statement.definition: RC2 and URC2: RC and URC with Cantor space replaced by {beta <=_1 gamma}; RB and URB: the corresponding statements that a function given by an associate is bounded on {beta <=_1 gamma} (uniformly via a type-3 functional for URB).
statement.facts: Corollary 4.2: over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{2,1}, each of RC2, URC2, RB, URB is equivalent to WKL.

statement.name: Explicit uniform fan theorem and uniform Heine-Borel lemma
statement.definition: UFAN(Phi): for all trees T <=_1 1 and g^2, if every beta <=_1 1 has beta g(beta) not in T then (forall beta <=_1 1)(exists i <= Phi(g)) beta i not in T. UHB(Psi) as above.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.2: terms s, t can be extracted from the proof of WKL <-> HB in RCA_0 witnessing the explicit equivalence FAN <-> HB in RCA_0^omega, i.e. forall Phi^3 [UFAN(Phi) -> UHB(s(Phi))] and forall Psi^3 [UHB(Psi) -> UFAN(t(Psi))].

statement.name: Nonstandard continuity of standard continuous functionals; existence of a modulus-of-continuity functional
statement.definition: Statements in the nonstandard system RCA_0^Omega (with predicate st): NC says every standard continuous Phi^2 is nonstandard continuous; MC says there is a standard type-3 modulus-of-continuity functional Psi.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.4: NC <-> MC in RCA_0^Omega. RCA_0^omega does not prove the existence of such a modulus functional (cited from Kohlenbach and Troelstra).

statement.name: Uniform diagonally non-recursive functions
statement.definition: (exists Psi^{1->1})(forall A^1)(forall e^0)(Psi(A)(e) != Phi_e^A(e)): a functional producing, from each A, a function DNR relative to A.
statement.facts: UDNR is equivalent to (exists^2), i.e. arithmetical comprehension (Theorems 4.6, 4.7: P proves UDNR+ <-> Pi01-TRANS, with an effective version relative to Feferman's mu^2).

statement.name: Uniform monotone convergence theorem
statement.definition: There is a functional t giving, for every bounded increasing sequence c of reals in [0,1] and k, a modulus of Cauchy convergence t(c)(k).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.1: uniform MCT is equivalent to Feferman's mu^2 (explicit terms extracted from the nonstandard equivalence MCT_ns <-> Pi01-TRANS).

statement.name: Perfect subtree theorem (every tree with uncountably many paths has a non-empty perfect subtree), uniform version
statement.definition: For all trees T, if T has uncountably many paths, t(T) is a non-empty perfect subtree of T (uniform functional t).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.4: the uniform version is equivalent to Feferman's mu^1 (the Suslin functional version), extracted from PST_ns <-> Pi11-TRANS; the non-uniform equivalence with Pi11-CA0 is attributed to Sakamoto-Yamazaki [32, Theorem 4.4].

statement.name: Gandy-Hyland functional
statement.definition: A type-3 functional with Gamma(Y,s) = Y(s*0*(lambda n)Gamma(Y,s*(n+1))) for continuous Y.
statement.facts: Corollary 5.2: expressible in terms of Feferman's mu^2 and the special fan functional (over E-PA^omega* + QF-AC^{1,0}); Corollary 5.3: also via a modulus-of-continuity functional.

statement.name: Special fan functional
statement.definition: A type-3 functional Theta such that for all g, binary tree T, if no alpha <= 1 in Theta(g)(2) has alpha g(alpha) in T then every beta <= 1 has beta i not in T for some i <= Theta(g)(1).
statement.facts: Theorem 5.6: computable from the intuitionistic fan functional; Theorem 5.7 (Normann): computable (S1-S9) from E^2-type xi; Theorem 5.8 (Normann): not S1-S9 computable in any type-2 functional.

statement.name: Finite subfamily of an open cover of [0,1] with measure of union > 1 - epsilon
statement.definition: If (I_n) is a cover of [0,1] by open intervals, then for every epsilon > 0 there is N such that mu(I_1 ∪ ... ∪ I_N) > 1 - epsilon.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WWKL in BISH (Proposition 10); implied by VCT.

statement.name: Spatiality of the formal topology R of formal reals
statement.definition: A formal topology is spatial if a C_Pt(A) U implies a C_A U (formal cover equals point-wise cover).
statement.facts: Spatiality of R is equivalent to the Heine-Borel property for Pt(R) restricted to covers by rational intervals (Proposition 17); spatiality for Vitali covers implies spatiality (Lemma 22).

statement.name: Modulus of pointwise continuity functional (fan functional for pointwise continuity)
statement.definition: (∃Δ³)(∀φ²)(∀f,g ≤₁ 1)[f̄Δ(φ,f) = ḡΔ(φ,f) → φ(f)=φ(g)]: a functional giving a modulus of pointwise continuity on Cantor space for every type-2 functional.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.1 (over RCA0^Omega): equivalent to nonstandard continuity principles (PC*), (PC). Theorem 6.1: over RCA0^omega, UFAN2 + (MPC) <-> (MUC); Theorem 6.3: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,0}, FAN + (MPC) <-> (MUC); Corollary 6.6 over RCA0^omega + (MPC) + QF-AC^{2,0}: FAN <-> UFAN2 <-> QF-FAN <-> (UQF) <-> (MUC). Not entered: (MPC) and QF-AC^{2,0} have no catalogue id.

statement.name: Uniform fan theorem (with g^2)
statement.definition: There is a functional Φ³ such that for T ≤₁ 1 and g², (∀α≤₁1)(ᾱg(α) ∉ T) → (∀α≤₁1)(∃n ≤ Φ(g,T))(ᾱn ∉ T).
statement.facts: Implied by (MUC); with (MPC) equivalent to (MUC) (Theorem 6.1); over RCA0^omega + (MPC) + QF-AC^{2,0} equivalent to FAN (Corollary 6.4, 6.6). UFAN1 (without g) is equivalent to (exists^2).

statement.name: Quantifier-free fan theorem
statement.definition: (∀f≤₁1)(∃n)A0(f,n) → (∃k)(∀f≤₁1)(∃n≤k)A0(f,n) for quantifier-free A0, and its uniform version (UQF).
statement.facts: Over RCA0^Omega + QF-AC^{2,0}: (MUC) <-> (UQF) <-> (UQF)^st <-> (Q) (Theorem 3.10); QF-FAN implies FAN; Corollary 6.5: QF-FAN + (MPC)_0 <-> (MUC) over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,0}.

statement.name: Supremum functional for type-2 functionals on Cantor space
statement.facts: Equivalent to (MUC) over RCA0^Omega + QF-AC^{2,0} (Theorem 3.8).

statement.name: Kohlenbach's uniform boundedness principle F and its uniform versions
statement.definition: (F): (∀Φ^{0→2},y^{0→1})(∃y'≤y)(∀k,z≤₁y(k)) Φ(k)(z) ≤ Φ(k)(y'(k)); (UF) its uniform version; (UCO) a uniform modulus of continuity on bounded domains for type 1→1 functionals.
statement.facts: (UF) <-> (UCO) <-> nonstandard versions over RCA0^Omega + QF-AC^{2,0} (Theorem 4.2); (UF) <-> (USB) (uniform Σ01-UB) (Theorem 4.4). Not related to catalogue statements.

statement.name: Brouwer's continuity theorem (every real function R→R is uniformly continuous on [0,1])
statement.definition: For every R→R function F (type 1→1 functional respecting equality of reals): (∀k)(∃N)(∀x,y∈[0,1])(|x−y|<1/N → |F(x)−F(y)|<1/k); UBCT adds a functional outputting N.
statement.facts: Theorem 6.7: over RCA0^Omega + (MPC) + QF-AC^{2,0}, (MUC) <-> BCT^st <-> UBCT^st <-> FAN^st <-> UFAN2^st <-> T^st <-> UT^st <-> T^* and other nonstandard principles; internal versions equivalent over RCA0^omega + (MPC) + QF-AC^{2,0}. Not entered: (MPC) and QF-AC^{2,0} have no catalogue id; BCT is about all functions R→R, not continuous ones, so it is not ucont.

statement.name: Modulus-of-continuity functional for type-2 functionals (Troelstra's C-N) and uniform weak continuity
statement.definition: (CONT): (∃Ψ³)(∀φ²,f,g)(f̄Ψ(φ,f) = ḡΨ(φ,g) → φ(f)=φ(g)); (UWC) the uniform version of WC-N.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.5: equivalent to nonstandard continuity principles over RCA0^Omega. Related to wcn but not the same statement.

statement.name: Π¹₁-Transfer principle (nonstandard)
statement.definition: (∀st f^1)[(∀st g^1)(∃st x^0) f(gx) ≠ 0 ↔ (∀g^1)(∃x^0) f(gx) ≠ 0], the Transfer principle of Nelson-style nonstandard analysis limited to Π¹₁-formulas; Π⁰₁-TRANS is the analogue for Π⁰₁-formulas.
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^Ω, Π⁰₁-TRANS is equivalent to (∃²) (Theorem 3, from van den Berg-Sanders), and Π¹₁-TRANS to (µ¹); over RCA†₀ + (STP2) + QF-AC^{1,1} it is equivalent to the Suslin functional (S²) and to (PB) (Theorem 11). All over nonstandard base systems, not RCA_0^ω.

statement.name: Stratified bounding principle for Π¹₁-formulas (search through the reals)
statement.definition: There is h^0 ⊐ 0 such that for f ⊑ 0, h ≥ h0 and M ⊐ h: (∀st g)(∃st x)(f(gx) ≠ 0) ↔ (∀g ≤* hM)(∃x ≤ M)(f(gx) ≠ 0).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-TRANS and, with QF-AC^{1,1}, to the Suslin functional (S²), over RCA†₀ + (STP2) (Theorem 11).

statement.name: Stratified bounding principles for Δ¹₁-formulas
statement.definition: Analogues of (PB) for formulas D(f,g) expressing that f, g give a Δ¹₁-formula, using the lexicographically least sequence P(k,h,M) of length M.
statement.facts: Over RCA†₀ + (STP2) + QF-AC^{1,1}, (D²) ↔ (SB) ↔ (TB) ↔ Δ¹₁-TRANS (Theorem 20); here (D²) is the functional version of Δ¹₁-CA (not the catalogue's third-order Δ-CA).

statement.name: Δ¹₁-Transfer principle (nonstandard)
statement.facts: Equivalent to the functional version (D²) of Δ¹₁-comprehension over RCA_0^Ω + (STP) + QF-AC^{1,1} (Theorem 16).

statement.name: Standard Part principles
statement.facts: RCA_0^Ω + (STP) proves WKL (Theorem 4); (STP) is conservative over WKL_0 (cited from van den Berg-Briseid, Keisler). Nonstandard base, so not entered over rca0.

items.concerns: Proved over EL0 (constructive base weaker than BISH); implications there hold in BISH. FAN is for detachable bars of binary sequences, matching fandelta.

statement.name: Existence of the limit superior and inferior of a bounded sequence of reals
statement.definition: Every bounded sequence of reals has a lim sup (and lim inf), defined by a in R is the lim sup of (x_n) iff for all k, m there is n>m with |a-x_n|<=1/(k+1), and there is l with x_j <= a+1/(k+1) for all j>l.
statement.facts: The paper lists it among principles implying arithmetical comprehension (introduction, item 5); in Section 5.6 shows single instances reduce to an arithmetical Pi^0_5 principle with bound in the fragment T_1 of Goedel's T.

statement.name: Principle of uniform Sigma^0_1-boundedness
statement.definition: For purely existential A, if for all y and all k, x<=y(k) there is z with A(x,y,k,z), then there is a type-1 functional bounding the witnesses uniformly (formula given in the introduction).
statement.facts: Implied by the axiom F over G_2A^omega + AC^{1,0}-qf; used to prove uniform continuity, attainment of the maximum, Heine-Borel, Dini; not provable in G_nA^omega.

statement.name: Convergence of bounded monotone sequences, Cauchy form without modulus
statement.definition: For every decreasing sequence a of reals in R+, for all k there is n with |a(m)-a(n)|<=1/(k+1) for all m>n.
statement.facts: The paper states PCM_1 is equivalent, relative to G_3A^omega (a weak base without quantifier-free choice), to second-order Sigma^0_1-induction.

statement.name: Π1-transfer (nonstandard analysis)
statement.definition: For all Δ0 formulas φ: (∀n ∈ N)φ(n) → (∀n ∈ *N)*φ(n), in the nonstandard base theory NSA (stratified nonstandard analysis, Definition 4 and Section 3).
statement.facts: Theorem 11: over NSA, LPO (read with the paper's hyperconnectives: for Σ1 P, P hyper-or hyper-not P) is equivalent to Π1-TRANS. Theorem 15: over NSA, LPO (hyper-version) is equivalent to LPR (hyper-version). Theorem 18: over NSA, MCT (stated with hyperimplication) is equivalent to LPO (hyper-version). All are in the paper's hyperconnective reading, not the classical or constructive reading of these principles.

statement.name: Π1-transfer limited to N1
statement.definition: Π1-TRANS with *N replaced by N1 in (5): (∀n ∈ N)φ(n) → (∀n ∈ N1)φ(n) for Δ0 φ.
statement.facts: Theorem 22: over NSA, MP (hyper-version) is equivalent to MPR (hyper-version) and to (Π1-TRANS)_1. The text states MP is strictly weaker than LPO (hyper-versions) over NSA, with models only sketched.

statement.name: Uniform continuity theorem for bounded functions
statement.definition: Every bounded, continuous function f : [a,b] -> R is uniformly continuous (pointwise continuity, constructive).
statement.facts: Lemma 5: BUCT[0,1] implies AS[0,1] (hence POS); Proposition 6: BUCT[0,1] implies UCT[a,b]; UCT => BUCT[a,b] => LUCT[a,b]; Proposition 7: LUCT[0,1] implies BUCT[0,1]; all over BISH.

statement.name: Locally uniform continuity theorem
statement.definition: Every continuous function of a compact metric space into a metric space is locally uniformly continuous.
statement.facts: Equivalent to UCT (UCT => LUCT => LUCT[0,1] => UCT, Proposition 7 and Proposition 6); equivalent to Strong Picard's Theorem (Theorem 22), all over BISH.

statement.name: Uniform differentiation theorem
statement.definition: Every differentiable function on [0,1] is uniformly continuously differentiable.
statement.facts: UCT => UDT => AS[0,1] (Proposition 18); whether the reverse implications hold is open.

statement.name: Strong Picard's Theorem (pointwise continuous defining function)
statement.definition: Picard existence theorem for y'=f(x,y), f only continuous and Lipschitz in y, giving a unique uniformly continuously differentiable local solution.
statement.facts: Theorem 22: equivalent to LUCT over BISH, hence to UCT.

statement.name: Peano's Theorem with uniformly continuous right-hand side
statement.definition: Peano existence theorem for f uniformly continuous on a rectangle, with a continuously differentiable solution on [x0-h,x0+h].
statement.facts: Stated to be equivalent to LLPO over BISH, citing Beeson [4] and Bridges [10] (no number given); definition differs from catalogue peano-ode (continuous f), so not entered.

statement.name: Strong Peano's Theorem
statement.definition: For f continuous, existence of an equicontinuous convergent sequence of approximate solutions iff existence of a uniformly continuously differentiable solution.
statement.facts: Theorem 27: equivalent to UCT over BISH.

statement.name: Standard Part (nonstandard compactness of Cantor space)
statement.definition: (forall alpha <=_1 1)(exists^st beta <=_1 1)(alpha ≈_1 beta): every binary sequence is infinitely close to a standard one; formulated in the nonstandard system B0 (fragments of IST over E-EFA^omega + QF-AC^{1,0}).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.2: equivalent in B0^- to (3.1) and (3.2); B0^- proves (exists^st Theta)SCF(Theta) -> STP. Theorem 3.4: B0 + (FF) + QF-AC^{2,1} proves STP <-> (exists Theta)SCF(Theta), while B0^- + (exists^3) + QF-AC does not. Theorem 3.5: B0 + QF-AC^{2,1} proves STP <-> HBU <-> HBU^st, B0^- + (exists^3) + QF-AC does not. Corollary 3.7: B0^- proves LUB^st -> HBU^st -> STP. Theorem 3.10: in B0^- + WWKL, STP <-> LMP <-> STP^-. These are over nonstandard base theories with no catalogue id, so no fact was entered.

statement.name: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL
statement.definition: (forall T <=_1 1)(mu(T) >> 0 -> (exists^st beta <=_1 1)(forall^st m)(beta m in T)), where mu(T) >> 0 is [mu(T) >_R 0]^st.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.9: B0 + QF-AC^{2,1} proves LMP <-> MLR_ns <-> HBU_ml, and with (FF) also <-> (exists Lambda)WCF(Lambda). Theorem 3.10: in B0^- + WWKL, STP <-> LMP <-> STP^-. Nonstandard base, so no fact entered.

statement.name: Weak fan functional
statement.definition: (forall k, g^2, T <=_1 1)((forall alpha in Lambda(g,k)(2))(alpha g(alpha) not in T) -> (exists n <= Lambda(g,k)(1))(L_n(T) <= 1/k)), the functional arising from WWKL.
statement.facts: Equivalent to LMP over B0 + (FF) + QF-AC^{2,1} (Theorem 3.9).

statement.name: Standard version of HBU
statement.definition: HBU with all quantifiers relative to st.
statement.facts: B0 + QF-AC^{2,1} proves STP <-> HBU <-> HBU^st (Theorem 3.5); B0^- proves LUB^st -> HBU^st -> STP (Corollary 3.7).

statement.name: Uniform intermediate value theorem for functionals
statement.definition: ∃F: C → [0,1] ∀f ∈ C f(F(f)) =_R 0, where C is the space of f ∈ C[0,1] with f(0) ≤ 0, f(1) ≥ 0 (given as type 1→1 functionals extensional w.r.t. =_R).
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω, also restricted to Lipschitz functions with constant 1 (item 3).

statement.name: Uniform attainment of the maximum principle
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω, also restricted to Lipschitz functions with constant 1 (item 5).

statement.name: Uniform Brouwer fixed point theorem
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω, also restricted to Lipschitz functions with constant 1 (item 7).

statement.name: Functional ∃φ² selecting a point with f(φ(f))=0
statement.definition: (2): ∃²-existence together with a functional φ such that ∀f^1 (∃x f(x)=0 → f(φ(f))=0).
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) and UWKL over RCA₀^ω (Proposition 3.9).

statement.notation: existence of a not everywhere sequentially continuous functional (Prop 3.7)
statement.name: Non-sequentially continuous functional of type 2 or 1→1
statement.definition: There exists a functional of type 2 (or 1→1) which is not everywhere sequentially continuous (or not everywhere ε-δ-continuous).
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω (Grilliot's trick).

statement.name: Upper semi-continuous functions on [0,1] are bounded above
statement.definition: A usco function f : [0,1] -> R (Definition 2.2) is bounded above.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.5: over RCA_0^omega equivalent to the Heine-Borel theorem for sequences of open sets, the Cantor intersection theorem, attainment of the supremum for usco functions, HBC_s; over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} equivalent to WKL_0 and HBC. Corollary 2.27: equivalent to WKL_0 and the Lebesgue number lemma over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + B-Pi. Z_2^omega does not prove it.

statement.name: Heine-Borel theorem for closed sets and sequences of open sets
statement.definition: For closed C in [0,1] (third-order) and a sequence of open sets (O_n) covering C, finitely many O_n cover C. HBC is the restriction to basic open intervals.
statement.facts: Item (f) of Theorem 2.5, equivalent over RCA_0^omega to usco functions being bounded above; HBC equivalent to WKL_0 over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}; Z_2^omega does not prove HBC.

statement.name: Sequential Cantor intersection theorem
statement.definition: For a double sequence of non-empty closed sets C_{n,m} in [0,1] with C_{n+1,m} contained in C_{n,m}, there is a sequence (y_m) with y_m in the intersection over n of C_{n,m}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL_0 + ClC over RCA_0^omega (Theorem 2.8).

statement.notation: Lebesgue number lemma for sequences of open sets
statement.name: Lebesgue number lemma (third-order open sets)
statement.definition: For a sequence of open sets covering [0,1] there is k such that every interval of length below 2^-k lies in some O_n.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.25); equivalent to WKL_0 over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + B-Pi (Corollary 2.27).

statement.name: Induction principle IND1 (finite choice for unique functions in Cantor space)
statement.facts: A special case of finite choice; valid in the models of [24-30,32], so Z_2^omega + IND1 does not prove NBI. Used as an extra hypothesis in Theorem 2.2 (RCA_0^omega + IND1).

statement.name: Basic properties of continuous functions on unrepresented compact metric spaces (M,d), M a subset of R
statement.definition: Third-order statements such as: on a countably-compact (or sequentially compact) metric space a (sequentially) continuous F : M → R is bounded, uniformly continuous, has a supremum or a maximum; Dini's theorem; Pincherle's theorem; Ascoli-Arzela; equicontinuity implies uniform equicontinuity; sequentially compact implies strongly countably-compact, separable, sequential Cantor intersection property, limit point compact.
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega + IND1, items (a)-(g) and (h)-(t) each imply NBI[0,1] (Theorem 2.2, with the replacements of countably-compact by compact, complete and totally bounded, or strongly countably-compact); items (h)-(l) are provable in Z_2^Omega. Over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, items (h),(i),(m),(n),(o),(q),(s),(t) are provable (Theorem 2.4).

statement.name: Boundedness above of continuous functions / sequential compactness of weakly complete effectively totally bounded metric spaces M ⊂ [0,1]
statement.definition: (e.2): for any weakly complete and effectively totally bounded metric space (M,d) with M ⊂ [0,1], a continuous F : M → R is bounded above. (f.2): any such (M,d) is sequentially compact.
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega, WKL_0 is equivalent to (e.1)-(e.3) (e.3 for sequentially continuous functions) and ACA_0 is equivalent to (f.2). Without 'effectively' (e.3) implies NBI[0,1].

statement.name: Strong countable compactness of the unit interval; limit point compactness of weakly complete effectively totally bounded spaces
statement.definition: The unit interval is strongly countably-compact (every sequence of open sets covering it has a finite subcover); a weakly complete and effectively totally bounded (M,d), M ⊂ [0,1], is limit point compact.
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}: WKL_0 is equivalent to the unit interval being strongly countably-compact (proof of the equivalence cited to [28, Theorem 4.1]), and ACA_0 is equivalent to limit point compactness of such spaces.
